channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Hockenson did the same yesterday and can be safely expected to start in Week 7 against the Colts’ beatable defense. Hockenson has seemingly developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray and can be started as a fantasy football TE1 this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Buccaneers placed Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve with a finger injury.
item.description: Rozeboom heads to injured reserve with five tackles and one quarterback pressure to his name. The Buccaneers correspondingly activated David Sills from injured reserve-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice’s strain was only a “tweak” in his Week 4 post-game remarks. So much for that. The Chiefs will almost assuredly be without their No. 1 wide receiver against the Seahawks this week, leaving Xavier Worthy to handle the role.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Tyler Guyton (calf) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description: The Cowboys’ left tackle played through a minor back issue earlier this month as well. He’s a little banged up at the moment. Whether this injury keeps him out remains to be seen. The Cowboys take on the division-rival Eagles on Monday night.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description: Reliable ESPN beat reporter Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder during the Cowboys’ last two games. He does not think that this injury threatens Pickens’ Week 7 availability. Thanks, Todd. Ideally, Pickens jumps back up to full participation tomorrow, and we head into Sunday carefree. Stay tuned.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.-Nic Bodiford
